findings.gate: Charter §4.3 (costs persist across scenes and reconcile to the ledger); THE_AUTHOR Gate 13 (every injury or exhaustion state recurs or is explicitly resolved at the character's next appearance); craft core invariant 3

draft_evidence.quote: Oryn on the bank above the spring with her roll beside her and her hands on her knees, watching a man with a stick not sit down. Vastin standing, because he had been told he was spent and did not yet believe it, with the stick planted and his weight on it and his face the colour it had been on the road's stone, a day paler.

comparison_evidence.quote: And the knee's gone — not broken; gone the way a knee goes that's been asked to be a wall's foot on stone for as long as that was. That's the wound, and it's a real one, and it'll be a real one for a month. [...] Vastin, spent to the floor, and the knee — the wall's foot, on stone, for as long as it took — gone under him; Oryn bound it and said a month. That's the wound.

findings.consequence: Chapter 4's own repair pass gave Vastin a bound right knee, named by the healer as 'the wound', priced at a month, and entered in the log Cael closed the chapter on. Chapter 5 is the next morning and his next appearance, and the wound is not on the page: he is 'spent', his 'legs wanted more than that', and he carries the ash stick he has carried since he came off the ferry in Chapter 2 — so nothing in the chapter distinguishes a man who is tired from a man who was bound yesterday. The absence is loudest where the healer is: Oryn comes down off the bank at L15 to look at Brom's foot unasked, puts two fingers on the binding, says 'It'll walk', and goes back up without a glance at the knee she bound the day before. A reader coming straight off Chapter 4's injury ledger will register the knee as having quietly healed overnight, which is the exact failure §4.3 exists to prevent; Chapter 6 then reintroduces it as live ('I'll read the shoulder there and the knee there', ch06.md L89), so Chapter 5 is the one gap in the chain.
findings.repair_target: One clause, in any of three places, all outside fixed text. Cheapest: L7, 'watching a man with a bound knee and a stick not sit down' — which also sharpens why he will not sit. Or L3, 'Vastin's legs wanted more than that' → 'Vastin's knee wanted more than that'. Best of the three, because it pays Oryn's presence rather than merely stating the fact: extend L15's descent so that on her way back up she looks at the knee without being asked and says nothing about it, or says the healer's one word — which costs four words, keeps her silence about paper intact, and lets Vastin's refusal to sit at L119 land as a cost rather than a posture. Do not add a second injury beat for Brom's shoulder; Ch4 discharged that one and Ch6 carries it.

findings.category: internal arithmetic — the repair paragraph counts itself wrong
findings.gate: Craft core: causal legibility; charter §3.1 (the cataloguing narrator counts things and the counts hold); the packet's own plant-3 obligation, which is a beat about a count

draft_evidence.quote: She counted the second row twice, because she had handed Cael its last three sheets to hold flat against the wind while she weighted the others, and the row came out a sheet short with his three in his hands and a sheet right when he set them down, and she counted it a third time with the sheets on the stone and got the right number, and looked at his hands, once, and said nothing, and went on.

findings.consequence: The sentence opens by asserting two counts and then narrates three: the short count with the sheets in Cael's hands, the right count when he sets them down, and 'she counted it a third time'. The paragraph is the chapter's newly inserted Book-11 plant, and the whole of its evidential force depends on a reader trusting a tally — in a chapter whose narrator is defined by being 'a man who could not not count' and whose central beat is a man doing arithmetic correctly where an office rounded. A careful reader who checks the count, which this paragraph explicitly invites, finds the narration miscounting in the act of reporting a miscount. That undercuts the plant rather than planting it, and it is the one paragraph in the chapter with no r1 version to fall back on.
findings.repair_target: One word. Either 'She counted the second row twice' → 'She counted the second row three times' (which also front-loads the oddity and is truer to Karis, who re-checks), or 'She counted the second row again' with 'a third time' left standing, or drop 'and she counted it a third time with the sheets on the stone and got the right number' and let the second count be the confirming one. Prefer the first: the escalating tally is the tell, and Karis counting a row three times is characterisation Book 7 already established. While the paragraph is open, resolve the two secondary snags in it noted in concerns — 'a sheet right' as a parallel to 'a sheet short', and 'while she weighted the others', which reopens a weighting L11 has already completed.

findings.gate: Charter §6 (world discipline; established geography holds); charter §4.1's drawability standard applied to the road; craft core invariant 3

draft_evidence.quote: and then at the road's fork — a day on, past the rise, where a track went north to seven holds that owed her a visit — and did not look at it long [...] and the road going west past the spring toward a rise that had, on the far side of it, a city she had never seen

The track went north-west, off the kept surface and onto ruts

findings.consequence: L123 puts the fork beyond the rise; L127, four lines later, puts the city beyond the rise; and Chapter 6 puts the rise beyond the fork ('The road went on west over a long rise'), with Treswick beyond that again and reached on the 282nd. Read straight, Chapter 5 seats the fork and the city on the same far side of one rise, which would put Oryn's turning within sight of the walls — the opposite of the arrangement Chapter 6 builds its whole fork-stone scene on, and the opposite of what Chapter 7's countdown of wayposts needs. 'the rise' at L123 is also its first appearance in the chapter and carries a definite article with nothing behind it, so a listener has no way to attach it. The distance in the same clause is correct and must stay; it is only the ordering that is wrong.
findings.repair_target: Cut two words. L123: 'the road's fork — a day on, past the rise, where a track went north' → 'the road's fork — a day on, where a track went north'. The distance, which Chapter 6 depends on, is untouched, and L127's rise then stands alone as the one rise in the chapter with the city behind it. If a landmark is wanted in the clause, use the one Chapter 6 actually gives the fork — the gap in the hills that has the last light in it — rather than a rise. draft_evidence.quote: He noted it. He had a page for that now, and it was getting to be a page.

comparison_evidence.quote: I'm entering it as what it is: an observation I can't file. I've a page for those. It's getting long.

findings.consequence: The repair's closing clause is circular on its face — he had a page for it, and it was getting to be a page — so the sentence's own image cancels; a listener gets 'page' twice in nine words with no change of sense between them. It also pre-empts Karis's line twenty-four lines later, which is the chapter's established version of the move and lands better ('I've a page for those. It's getting long.'), so the new sentence spends the effect before the character whose habit it is arrives to use it. With L93's 'A day he had a page for', the chapter now runs three instances of 'a page for', which is the whole book's §9 budget spent in one chapter; ch14.md carries a fourth. Localized, but the friction sits in the last line of the paragraph that carries the chapter's new plant, where the reader should be looking at Cael's hands.
findings.repair_target: Rewrite the second clause off the word 'page'. 'He noted it. He had somewhere to put that now, and the somewhere was filling' keeps the accumulation without the echo; simpler still, cut to 'He noted it, and did not say so', which also matches Karis's silence in the same sentence and leaves L49 the only page line in that movement. Then re-run 'a page for' over the chapter — target two, not three — and over the book, where four exceeds §9's cap of three and wants a pass at ch14.md rather than here.

concerns: The r1 blockers are both closed and neither repair cost the chapter anything: the same-mark reading at L61-L65 is a stronger finding than the differing mark was, because it makes the office's indifference the point ('I don't know if the same mark means the same kind or only that the office had one mark'), and the five-years-and-a-hundred-some-days line at L91 gives Cael a reason to be exact that is also characterisation ('a marshal rounds; a cataloguer does not'). Preserve both formulations in any later pass.

L61's 'Twice the size and the same mark' can be read as the mark being twice the size or the site being twice the size. Brom's next line ('four hundred meters to its middle') and Karis's later 'why a thing twice the size gets the same mark' both resolve it to the site, so the chapter is consistent — but a listener meets the ambiguous version first, and DECISIONS row 15's phrase 'the fourth differs in size only' can be read either way too. Worth one clarifying word at L61 ('The fourth. The stroke and the bar. The same mark on a site twice the size.') and, more usefully, worth pinning the referent in the DECISIONS row before Ch17 and Ch20 decode the grade against it.

Two secondary snags inside the new L25 paragraph, best fixed in the same pass as F-B8-CH05-013: 'the row came out a sheet short with his three in his hands and a sheet right when he set them down' uses 'a sheet right' as a parallel to 'a sheet short', which is not a construction English supports and stumbles read aloud; and 'while she weighted the others' reopens a weighting L11 has already reported as complete ('weighted at the corners with stones from the trough'), so the sheets are being laid out twice.

Book-level capped-phrase counts, outside this chapter's scope but now inaccurate in the ledger: STATE_RUNNING's Ch1 closing note records one use of 'upside down' in Ch1 and one reserved for Ch8, and says the book cap is reached. Counted over the drafted files, ch01.md carries two in a single sentence at L141 and ch04.md and ch14.md carry one each, so the book stands at five or six against a cap of three. Ch5 is clean (zero) and is not the problem; the Ch1/Ch4/Ch14 counts want a book-level pass and a corrected ledger line.

THE_AUTHOR Gate 27 and the charter's Reader Standard both require that the author report state the reader standard was checked before a chapter is closed. reports/ch05-author-r2.json contains no such attestation and has no field carrying one. The chapter's content passes the gate on inspection, so this is a loop-procedure gap rather than a prose defect, but the gate as written is not satisfied until the attestation exists. Folded into F-B8-CH05-014's repair target so it can be closed in one edit.

The plant ledger at CHAPTER_ARCHITECTURE still specifies Book-11 plant 3 for Ch1 and Ch5 as 'the recovered survey kit's instruments return clean readings for everyone and errors or nulls in his hands'. Ch5 now delivers a record anomaly instead, which the r1 repair target sanctioned and STATE_RUNNING records. Amend the ledger line so the plant reconciles at the Continuity Checkpoint, and note while doing so that the escalation across the book currently reads flat — Ch1 is three instruments repeating a result, Ch5 is one miscount — where the ledger promises anomalies that 'increase across the book'. Ch14 and Ch22 carry the escalation, so this is a sequencing note, not a defect.

'A day and a half' at L137 is fixed text and correctly reproduced, and the packet asserts the same figure, so Ch5 is compliant. It does not reconcile with the drafted downstream: the fork stone is the evening of the 280th (ch06.md), the last waypost short of the river is the 281st, and the outer district is the 282nd — two days' walking from this halt, not a day and a half. Flag to the Ch6-Ch8 reconciliation rather than to this chapter.

Vastin's 'forty years' (L51, L111) against the fifty-three the Ch2 correction fixed him at implies a career begun at thirteen. The phrase is card-fixed at Ch2's close and unchanged since r1, so it is not this chapter's to move, but it is the same class of seam as the one just repaired at L91 and is worth a decision at the planning layer before Book 9 stages his arc.

The container's noun now varies across three consecutive chapters: ch04.md L27 has 'the records flat in their oilcloth', ch05.md L125 has 'the flat case they had come in' and then 'the case' twice, and ch06.md L11 returns to 'the flat under her arm'. The F-B8-CH05-004 repair required the shift and 'flat case' bridges it honestly, so nothing here is wrong; but the oilcloth has disappeared without being opened, and 'the case' shares a scene with 'the kit's case' under Brom's foot at L7. One mention of the oilcloth coming off at the top of the halt would close both, cheaply.

The chapter labels its findings 'The grade second' (L57) and 'The third thing' (L77) while delivering instruments, the margin note, the grade and then the sheet — so the margin note, which the card lists as the third finding, arrives inside the first movement. The internal enumeration is self-consistent and the obligations do not fix an order, so this is not a defect; recording it only so a later pass does not 'correct' the numbering into a contradiction.
strengths: The two blocker repairs are surgical and additive rather than defensive. L91's 'Six was the marshal's rounding and the office's, and a marshal rounds; a cataloguer does not' converts a continuity fix into the clearest single statement of what Cael is that the chapter contains, and it does it in the same breath as the arithmetic the packet forbids him to say out loud.

The same-mark resolution at L61-L65 is the better finding, exactly as the r1 repair target predicted. 'I don't know if the same mark means the same kind or only that the office had one mark' and 'I can't see why a thing twice the size gets the same mark' leave Karis with a sharper unanswerable than the differing mark ever gave her, and 'Two copies of one ignorance' survives intact on top of it.

The discipline around the Book 9 sentence is unchanged and still the best thing in the chapter: Karis's clause dying mid-image at L41 ('the way a hundred lamps go out when — '), the ruler line reached for as a tool rather than recited at L45, and Vastin's 'You've said that before' / 'I say it when I need it' at L47-L49, which makes the discipline cost something to use.

L99's sentence — the sum done twice more, the log unopened, the sheet put back 'with its head turned like the row's other heads, so that it lay in the file as if it had never been out of it' — pays Seln's Ch3 silence in physical action and nothing else, and L103's 'the first thing he had ever owned that he had not written down, and he found that he could carry it' is the chapter's progression delta stated once and then dropped.

Seln's teaching beat holds its shape through three separate substitutions. 'Two,' Seln said, to nobody' at L69 is the whole tally mechanism installed in four words, and 'Escalate it ... That's the word. Directive, classification, escalation. I've been counting. Three.' now verifies against the page instead of asking the reader to take it on trust.

L111 does real work with one preposition: Vastin's 'up' unpacked through Cael's own history under it — 'He had said *up* about Cael once, at seventeen, in a room with a table, and the thing had gone up, and had come back down as a designation' — so the man's third reflex indicts him without anyone at the spring saying so.

The eleven local substitutions are genuinely local. 'the time the wind takes to lift a sheet's corner and let it fall' at L33 replaces a capped phrase with the halt's own furniture and improves the interval; 'the wind was at their backs' at L3 is plainer than what it replaced; and no fixed line, no obligation beat and no strength identified at r1 was disturbed to make room for any of them.
